analysis.one_liner: Tata Consumer Products sells packaged tea, coffee, salt and foods (Tata Tea, Tetley, Tata Salt, Tata Sampann) in India and abroad, and runs Tata Starbucks and NourishCo as growth bets alongside its legacy beverages business.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (quarter ended September 2026, reported 26 October 2026) showed consolidated revenue up 14% to ₹5,661 crore, EBITDA up 18% to ₹794 crore (margin +40bps to 14.0%), and net profit up 16% to ₹470 crore. The growth businesses - Tata Sampann, ready-to-drink beverages, Capital Foods and Organic India - grew 40% collectively and now make up 38% of the India business, while core Indian tea volumes stayed flat and the UK Tetley business fell on a heatwave-hit category. The company also completed buying out the remaining stake in Capital Foods, taking its holding to around 80%.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a tea-and-salt company trying to turn itself into a broader packaged foods and beverages company, and the growth businesses (ready-to-eat snacks, Sauce brand Capital Foods, RTD drinks, Starbucks) are growing fast and now matter more to the numbers than tea does. The tension: the stock trades at roughly 57 times earnings - a steep premium for an FMCG company - while its return on equity is only around 7%, well below what that price tag normally implies. You are paying up front for the newer businesses to keep compounding; if tea margins or the newer bets disappoint, the multiple has little cushion.
analysis.quarters: Revenue growth has been running at double digits for several quarters, driven increasingly by the growth portfolio (Tata Sampann +57%, RTD +47%, Starbucks +15% this quarter) rather than core tea and salt, where India tea/coffee revenue was roughly flat and industry-wide tea volumes actually fell ~6% (so TCPL held share rather than grew volume there). Management took tea pricing up 8-10% through the year to pass on leaf-cost inflation, and said the full margin benefit of tea and salt price hikes will show up in Q3 FY27. International revenue grew 7% reported but fell 2% in constant currency - UK/Tetley was hit by a heatwave denting category demand, while US and Canada grew. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 50-70bps of EBITDA margin expansion and a longer-term (3-5 year) target of 17-20% India EBITDA margin, well above the current 14%, meaning the market is pricing in margin improvement that has not yet shown up in reported numbers.
analysis.performance_read: Only one stock split is on record (10:1, back in 2010), so the recent price fall is not a corporate-action artifact - the stock is genuinely down about 19% from its 11 May 2026 peak of ₹1,260 to ₹1,021, and down 12.5% over one year (slightly worse than the Nifty's -12%, but far better than the chosen FMCG peer HUL at -24% over one year). Over 3 and 5 years the stock has essentially tracked the Nifty - 17% vs 20% over 3 years, 31% vs 30% over 5 years - meaning Tata Consumer has not meaningfully outperformed the broad market despite the growth-business narrative, though it has decisively beaten HUL, which is down over both periods.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 57x, the stock is priced well above typical FMCG multiples (25-35x), and the premium is explicitly a bet on the growth businesses and margin expansion continuing, not a reflection of current profitability - ROE is only about 7% and ROCE about 9%, both below large-cap FMCG peers. Whether that premium is justified depends on whether margins actually climb toward management's 17-20% long-term target; right now the multiple is running ahead of the return ratios that would normally support it.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is now clearly margin-and-mix led as much as volume led: overall revenue growth of 14% is increasingly driven by the higher-growth, higher-margin newer businesses (Sampann, RTD, Capital Foods, Starbucks, up 40% collectively) while the original commodity businesses - tea and salt - are closer to flat in volume, with pricing (8-10% tea price hikes) doing more of the work than units sold. That makes the growth more durable than a pure commodity-price story, but it also means a large chunk of reported growth is still recently acquired (Capital Foods, Organic India) rather than organic.
analysis.health_read: Balance sheet is conservative - cash of about ₹4,863 crore against debt of about ₹2,820 crore, a net cash position with debt/equity near 0.1 - so financial risk is low. The more relevant risk is business/margin risk: current EBITDA margin (14%) sits well short of management's own 17-20% medium-term target, and low ROE/ROCE suggest capital (including goodwill from acquisitions like Capital Foods) is not yet earning a strong return. Cash conversion from profit was not independently verified in this search - check operating cash flow vs PAT on Screener before relying on it.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (Tata group) hold about 33.8% as of the most recent disclosed pattern, with zero pledging reported consistently since at least January 2024 - a clean promoter record. FIIs hold roughly 8.8% and DIIs about 25.3%, with the rest public. No specific marquee individual investor (e.g., a well-known value investor) was found on the register in this search; if you were expecting one, it does not appear to be there - not verified beyond this, check the latest shareholding pattern filing on the company's site for named investors above 1%.
strengths: Net cash balance sheet (~₹4,863 cr cash vs ~₹2,820 cr debt, debt/equity ~0.1)
Growth businesses (Sampann, RTD, Capital Foods, Organic India) grew 40% and now ~38% of India revenue, up from a smaller base
Held tea market share despite industry volumes falling ~6%, while still pushing through 8-10% price hikes
Zero promoter pledging on record since at least 2024, and 3-5 year stock returns in line with or ahead of the chosen FMCG peer (HUL)
watchpoints: ROE (~7%) and ROCE (~9%) are low for a stock priced at ~57x earnings - the valuation assumes margin expansion that has not yet materialized in reported numbers
Core tea volumes are flat and UK Tetley revenue fell on weak category demand (heatwave-related) - the legacy business is not growing in volume terms
EBITDA margin (14.0%) still well below management's own 17-20% medium-term target - a multi-year execution gap, not a near-term fix
Stock is down ~19% from its May 2026 peak and has only matched the Nifty over 3-5 years, despite the growth-business story
analysis.one_thing: Whether EBITDA margin actually moves toward management's 50-70bps FY27 guidance (with full tea/salt price-hike benefit expected in Q3 FY27) - that single data point will show whether the 57x multiple is being earned or is running ahead of the business.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked Q2 FY27 numbers (revenue, EBITDA, PAT, growth-business performance, management guidance) across multiple independent news sources (Business Standard, Investing.com, GuruFocus/Yahoo earnings-call highlights, PSU Connect) that were consistent with each other. Valuation ratios (P/E ~57x, ROE ~7-7.4%, ROCE ~9-9.4%, debt figures) are drawn from aggregator sites (Screener-linked summaries, MoneyWorks4Me, Tijori) and were broadly consistent across sources but not independently verified against the company's own filings - treat as approximate and recheck on Screener. Shareholding pattern (33.83% promoter, zero pledge) sourced from Trendlyne/Choice India aggregation of the company's own BSE/NSE filings. Cash flow-to-profit conversion was not verified and is flagged as such in health_read. Market price, returns and corporate-action data were supplied and used as given, not recomputed.
